name: Museu de Marinha (Maritime Museum)
seoTitle: Museu de Marinha, Belém: Royal Barges on a Port Day
tagline: The Navy's museum in the west wing of Jerónimos, best for ship models, royal barges and the 1922 Santa Cruz seaplane

description.short: The Portuguese Navy's museum, in the west wing of the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém. About 2,500 objects are on display, from Discoveries-era ship models and navigation instruments to royal barges and early seaplanes. Adult entry is €8.
description.full:
The Museu de Marinha is the natural second stop in Belém once you have seen the Jerónimos Monastery, because it occupies the monastery's west wing, with its own entrance at the western end of the building. It is about 7.5 km from the Jardim do Tabaco terminal: a taxi takes 15 to 20 minutes, tram 15E runs from Praça do Comércio to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop, and the Cascais-line train from Cais do Sodré stops at Belém station.

Plan on 60 to 90 minutes inside. If you are short of time, go straight to the Discoveries rooms near the entrance (ship models, astrolabes and the carved figure of the Archangel Raphael said to have sailed with Vasco da Gama), then cross to the Barge Pavilion. That hall holds six royal barges, five of them 18th-century, the largest built in 1780, plus traditional working boats and three naval seaplanes, including the Santa Cruz that made the first aerial crossing of the South Atlantic in 1922. The later rooms on the merchant fleet and the modern Navy are the ones to skip if you are pressed.

Opening times catch people out. From 1 October to 31 May the museum is closed on Monday mornings and opens at 13:00, and the monastery next door is closed all day on Mondays, so a Monday call in winter or spring leaves Belém thin in the morning. Otherwise it opens at 10:00 daily, closing at 17:00 (last entry 16:30) from October to April and at 18:00 (last entry 17:30) from May to September.

At €8 for adults it costs less than half the Jerónimos cloister, and it is far quieter: mid-morning, when tour groups fill the monastery, is a good time to come here instead. Entry is free on the first Sunday of each month until 14:00, which brings more local families. Tripods and artificial lighting are not allowed.
description.history: The museum was created by decree on 22 July 1863 on the initiative of King Luís I, who had trained as a naval officer. It was first housed beside the Naval School, and a large fire at the old Navy Arsenal in 1916 destroyed much of the early collection. In 1948 the collector Henrique Maufroy de Seixas donated more than 300 pieces on condition that they be shown in a suitable building, so in April 1949 the museum reopened provisionally in the Farrobo palace at Laranjeiras. On 15 August 1962 it opened in the north and west wings of the Jerónimos Monastery, alongside a new pavilion built for the royal barges.
description.significance: It is the Portuguese Navy's own museum and holds more than 18,000 objects, of which around 2,500 are on display. For a visitor in Belém it fills a gap the monuments leave: the monastery and tower show what the sea route to India paid for, while this collection shows the ships, instruments and boats that made it possible, through to the 20th-century Navy and naval aviation.

directions.general: Located in the Belém district, adjacent to the Jerónimos Monastery, one of Lisbon's most iconic landmarks
directions.fromCruisePort: About 7.5 km west, in the west wing of the Jerónimos Monastery. Taxi 15-20 minutes, tram 15E from Praça do Comércio to the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos stop, or the train from Cais do Sodré to Belém.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 15E to Belém. Bus routes 727, 28, 729, 714, 751. Train to Belém station from Cais do Sodré. Metro to Cais do Sodré, then tram 15E.
directions.parking: Limited street parking in Belém. Use Jerónimos Monastery parking or Belém Cultural Centre car park (5-minute walk)

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily; closed on Monday mornings from 1 October to 31 May

admissionPrices.notes: 2026 Navy price list (Despacho 1/2026): adults 13-64 €8; children 4-12 €4; seniors 65+ €4; children 0-3 free; family (2 adults + 2 children) €21, extra child €3. Museum + Navy Planetarium €12 adult. Free on the first Sunday of each month until 14:00, on 18 May (International Museum Day), 20 May (Navy Day), 22 July (Museum Day) and, for children 4-12, on 1 June.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Late morning, while tour groups are inside the Jerónimos cloister. Avoid Monday mornings from October to May, when the museum is closed until 13:00.
busyPeriods: First Sunday of the month (free until 14:00)
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Entrance is at the western end of the Jerónimos building, separate from the monastery. Prioritise the Discoveries rooms and the Barge Pavilion. Tripods and artificial lighting are not allowed. Tickets can be bought online at bilheteiracultura.marinha.pt.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 2.5-3 hours return from the ship for the museum alone; 4-5 hours if combined with the Jerónimos Monastery and Pastéis de Belém
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Not walkable from the ship (7.5 km). Taxi 15-20 minutes, tram 15E or the Cascais-line train to Belém. Inside, ramps and a lift serve the galleries.
tips: From 1 October to 31 May the museum opens only at 13:00 on Mondays, and the Jerónimos Monastery is closed all day; on a Monday call, plan Belém for the afternoon.
Adult entry is €8 and seniors 65+ pay €4, so it is a cheap add-on to the €18 Jerónimos cloister.
Go to the Barge Pavilion even if you skip the rest: the royal barges and the 1922 Santa Cruz seaplane are the museum's main draw.
Last admission is 30 minutes before closing: 16:30 from October to April, 17:30 from May to September.
Entry is free on the first Sunday of each month until 14:00; expect more families that morning.
Tripods and photographic lighting are not allowed; handheld photos are fine.
Tram 15E stops at Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, a few steps from the museum entrance at the west end of the monastery.
A family ticket (2 adults + 2 children aged 4-12) costs €21.

highlights: Discoveries-era ship models and navigation instruments, including astrolabes
Carved figure of the Archangel Raphael associated with Vasco da Gama's 1497 voyage
Barge Pavilion with six royal barges, five of them 18th-century; the largest dates from 1780
Fairey III seaplane Santa Cruz, used for the first aerial crossing of the South Atlantic in 1922
FBA Schreck seaplane of 1917 and a Grumman Widgeon from the last years of naval aviation
Traditional working boats: a Douro valboeiro, an Aveiro moliceiro, an Azorean whaleboat and a cod-fishing dory
Rooms on the merchant fleet, cod fishing and the modern Portuguese Navy
facilities: Wheelchairs on loan during the visit
Event spaces in the Barge Pavilion

accessibility.mobilityNotes: The museum states it meets EU accessibility standards, with ramps and a lift; wheelchairs can be borrowed for the visit.
